sections.h2: Who sends and collects the bill
sections.html:
Three offices handle county tax here, and Memphis adds a second bill. The Assessor of Property puts a value on each parcel. The County Commission picks the county rate. The Trustee multiplies that rate against every $100 of assessed value and mails the notice to the address on the Assessor's records. A lender that escrows your taxes can look up the details and pay for you, so the notice may only be a file copy.

  • Trustee: 157 Poplar Avenue, 2nd Floor, Memphis, TN 38103, (901) 222-0200. Counter hours are weekdays, eight to half past four. Payments by post go to P.O. Box 2751, Memphis, TN 38101-2751.
  • Board of Equalization: 1075 Mullins Station Road, Suite C-142, Memphis, TN 38134, (901) 222-7300.
  • City of Memphis Treasury: 125 North Main Street, 901-522-1111, for the separate city bill.

Write down each parcel number you own. When a notice goes missing, find the bill on the Trustee's realty tax page using the parcel number.

The county counted 910,226 people in July 2025, a 2.1% dip from the 2020 estimates base, living in 409,202 housing units. Owners occupy 54.1% of them. Median home value for 2020 to 2024 is $249,100, and 1,230 building permits were issued in 2025. About 46 percent of homes are rented, which means a landlord selling a rental often has tax and tenant questions an owner-occupant skips. Memphis is the county seat. Bartlett, Germantown, Lakeland, Millington, Arlington and Collierville run their own governments, and some of them send separate tax bills.

More than 353,000 real estate parcels are valued by the Assessor, who reappraises every fourth year. 2025 was the most recent round, 2029 is next, and business personal property is revalued annually. Market value is estimated from sales, cost and income data fed into a computer-assisted mass appraisal system.

The state then converts that value into a tax base with a fixed ratio: houses and farms are counted at one quarter of appraised value, and commercial and industrial parcels at 40 percent. The rate is applied to each hundred dollars of that base, and your notice prints the county rate. Within Memphis, the council fixes the city rate and city levies rely on the Assessor's certified values as of each January 1.

This year county bills could be paid starting Monday, October 5, and stay open through February's end. On March 1 the account is delinquent and a charge of 1.5 percent of the base tax lands every month until you pay. A mailed payment needs a postmark on or before the last day of February. Installments are fine. Memphis keeps its own calendar: it bills after the City Council sets a rate in mid to late June, and the tax is late once August 31 passes.

Delinquency dates and penalties by taxing body
Taxing bodyDelinquent onCharge
Shelby County, Arlington, Collierville, Lakeland, MillingtonMarch 11.5% a month, 18% a year
MemphisSeptember 11.5% a month, 18% a year
BartlettMarch 11.5% interest plus a 5% penalty in month one, then 1.5% a month
GermantownMarch 15% penalty at first, then 1% interest plus smaller penalties through July, then 1% a month

Selling a Memphis house means paying off both the county and the city account, so request two payoff figures, one from the Trustee and one from the City Treasury.

You petition the Shelby County Board of Equalization, the body that reviews the Assessor's values, and there is no fee. Appeals are heard in a window from May 1 to June 30 each year, and the outcome can be a higher value, a lower one, or no change. Miss the window and the disputed value usually stands for the year.

There are three ways to file: the Board's e-file site, a postmarked letter, or a visit to the Board's office on a weekday. The e-file site is live only during appeal season and takes uploaded supporting documents. You will get a hearing notice at least two weeks before the date. Moving a hearing is generally impractical, and every document you rely on must be in hand when you appear. Procedural questions go to (901) 222-7300.

sections.h2: Payment help for fixed-income and delinquent owners
sections.html:
The Trustee's Quarterly Payment Program is meant for retired or unemployed owners aged 65 and over on a fixed income, living in their own Memphis or Shelby County home with no delinquent taxes. Reapply each year, with applications taken July through October. County installments land on October 31, January 31, April 30 and July 31, and Memphis installments on August 31, November 30, February 28 and May 31.

A Written Payment Plan is a different tool for owners who are already delinquent. To qualify, the parcel has to be scheduled for a current tax sale, every delinquent year goes into the plan, the term tops out at 24 months, and each monthly payment is due by the 20th. Call the Tax Sale Department at (901) 222-0200. Older Memphis homeowners can also ask about the city's Tax Relief and Tax Freeze programs. The State of Tennessee resets the income limit annually.

Every payoff is checked by the Trustee the day the money comes in, and the lien stays until the balance is fully paid. That is why a closing agent should order a new payoff figure rather than reuse an old one. Interest is totaled through each month's end, but legal fees can be added mid-month, so a closing near the turn of a month deserves care.

State law directs the Trustee to sue for delinquent real estate tax. Memphis turns real estate accounts over to its delinquent attorneys on February 1 once they are a full year behind. If you are behind, call before that date. A quick cash closing can also help, because the lien gets paid from proceeds before more fees pile up.

Seasonal Trustee branches operate in Bartlett, Germantown, Arlington, Collierville, Millington and Raleigh. Year-round payment is at 157 Poplar Avenue, by phone at (901) 222-0200, or by mail.

Pull together the parcel number, your latest notice and proof of any payment plan or exemption before listing. Give copies to the closing agent so the payoff request names the correct county and city accounts.

faqs.q: When is Shelby County property tax due?
faqs.a: You could start paying Monday, October 5, and February's end is the cutoff. March 1 makes it delinquent, and 1.5 percent of the base tax is then added every month.

faqs.q: Does Memphis send a separate property tax bill?
faqs.a: Yes, the city bills separately once the City Council sets its rate, generally in mid to late June, and late status begins after August 31. For the city balance call the City Treasury at 901-522-1111. The Trustee handles the county balance.

faqs.q: When can I appeal my Shelby County property value?
faqs.a: During the May 1 to June 30 window. The Board of Equalization's online filing site works only in that season, so call (901) 222-7300 to confirm the dates for the current year.

faqs.q: How often does Shelby County reappraise?
faqs.a: Real property is reappraised on a four-year cycle, last in 2025 and next in 2029. Business personal property gets a new appraisal each year.

faqs.q: Can I set up a payment plan for delinquent Shelby County taxes?
faqs.a: Only if the parcel is scheduled for a current tax sale. The plan has to include every delinquent year, run no longer than 24 months, and have payments in by the 20th monthly. The Tax Sale Department at (901) 222-0200 sets it up.
